# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +271
- **Deletions**: -121
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T19:54:44Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +271
- **Deletions**: -121
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T19:54:44Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336

    "summary": "fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners",
    "description": "## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +271
- **Deletions**: -121
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T19:54:44Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336

    "description": "## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336"

BUT there's a subtle race: the watchdog's check `if (!identical(_engine, armed)) return;` happens after `await Future.delayed(...)`. Dispose can happen DURING the delay. Sequence: watchdog awaits delay → dispose runs (sets _engine = null, disposes notifiers) → delay completes → identical check → _engine is null → return. Safe.

But there's another race: watchdog delay completes → checks identical → passes → reads `tree.value` → OK. Between identical check and `bootError.value = ...` there is no await, so it's atomic within the event loop — dispose cannot interleave. So after a restart of a broken-then-fixed widget: tree still null (old run never rendered), bootError still set (old run set it) → error card forever even though the widget now works. And even worse — for a healthy widget restart: tree.value is old (non-null) → watchdog returns; but that's fine because tree renders.

Actually wait — there's a deeper issue with restart + tree: `onRender: (t) => tree.value = t` — the new engine sets tree when it renders. Between restart and first render of the new engine, tree.value holds the STALE tree from the old engine → the view would render the old UI even though the engine restarted. That's pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this PR. But bootError: once set, never cleared — that IS introduced by this PR. Let me check whether restart is a real path: grep for restart in app_tile_host / js_app_view / dynamic_widget_tile.

4. `AppLog.i` with 'WARNING: ' prefix — check if AppLog has .w. Let me check the AppLog class.

5. `ValueNotifier<Object?> bootError` — set with `StateError`. Using StateError as a message carrier is odd; a String would do. Minor suggestion.

6. In `js_app_view.dart`, the bootError card uses `context.l10n.appsStartError('$bootError', widget.app.name)` — need to verify the signature of appsStartError(message, appName). Let me check.

7. `@visibleForTesting` static mutable `uiTreeWarnAfter` — check import of foundation/proprietary. `visibleForTesting` is from flutter/foundation — js_app_engine.dart already uses `@visibleForTesting` (assembleEntryJsForTest), so import exists.

8. Watchdog armed AFTER `_replayStorageDrift()` — start() awaits several things; the 10s window starts after boot completes. Fine.

9. One more: `_watchUiTree` catches nothing — if `bootError.value = ...` throws (disposed notifier in debug — but guarded), or AppLog throws — unawaited error → unhandled async error in production. The identical guard makes notifier-dispose unlikely, but consider: the engine could be disposed and its notifiers disposed, then... _engine is nulled in dispose() before notifiers disposed; identical check reads `_engine` — null → return. Safe.

But WAIT: there's the `_guardLifecycle` serialization. `dispose()` runs inside `_guardLifecycle` — in production it goes through `_lifecycle` chain. `_engine = null` happens synchronously at the start of the action, so no serialization concern for the watchdog.

Another subtle thing: `_watchUiTree(_engine)` is passed `_engine` — at that point `_engine` was set to `engine` right after creation, so `_engine` non-null. Fine.

10. In the test: mutating static `JsAppEngine.uiTreeWarnAfter` then `finally` restore — but there are other tests in the file running in the same group that use the default; testWidgets runs sequentially, fine.

11. The test uses `waitFor(...)` — need to check the helper — with what timeout? If waitFor has a default timeout shorter than 400ms... let me check.

12. Potential flake: the test relies on real 400ms timers inside `tester.runAsync` — plus engine boot time. If boot takes >400ms on slow CI, then `broken.bootError` might be set before `await broken.start()` returns? Actually start() awaits `engine.run(js)` then arms the watchdog — the watchdog delay of 400ms starts after start() returns. But `healthy.start()` runs after; the broken watchdog timer fires 400ms after broken.start() returned. If healthy takes longer than 400ms to boot, bootError could already be set when we check — fine, waitFor handles both.

But here's a real flake risk: `expect(broken.tree.value, isNull)` immediately after start — could the broken widget have set tree? No — syntax error, never renders. OK.

The only new test is the engine-level watchdog. The UI surface changes (bootError → error card in 3 surfaces) have no widget-level tests. Is there existing coverage that would catch regressions? The change is straightforward wiring, but a test asserting bootError renders the error card in js_app_view would be valuable. That's an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION finding. Given the AC-first claim "AC test" covers the engine, the surfaces are untested. Let me check the existing tests for the surfaces to see the established patterns (e.g., app_tile_host_test has tests for failed boot → icon fallback?).

But WAIT — in dynamic_widget_tile, is the engine of type JsAppEngine? The canvas uses `engine` — let me read the file to check. There's a comment about `widget_tile.js` path. The canvas state builds `engine` — need to check the engine type there (JsAppEngine presumably).

15. `app_tile_host.dart` — the bootError branch shows AppIcon. But the PR description says fullscreen view shows "the existing start-error card". In app_tile_host there's already a start-error branch above (the diff hunk starts at line 355 with a preceding error card return). Let me read app_tile_host.dart fully around that area to see the existing start-error handling and confirm the new branch placement.

16. Backward compat: `bootError` is a new public field on JsAppEngine — additive, fine.

17. The watchdog fires even for engines whose start() succeeded but the app legitimately takes >10s to first render (e.g., heavy network fetch in bootstrap before jsr.render). Then a healthy-but-slow app shows a false error card. And since bootError is never cleared when tree later arrives, the false error sticks even after render. Hmm — but the views check bootError FIRST, so once bootError is set, even a later render never shows. This is a genuine correctness concern for slow-rendering apps: permanent error card despite eventual successful render. Mitigation: clear bootError in onRender (when tree arrives) — `onRender: (t) { bootError.value = null; tree.value = t; }`. That's a real improvement. Severity: IMPORTANT (not blocking — 10s is generous for first render, and the issue being fixed is infinite spinners; a slow app that renders at 12s would previously show a spinner forever-ish then work; now it shows an error card even after working). Actually with the current code: app renders at 12s → tree set at 12s → view shows... bootError set at 10s → error card. tree.value != null but the view never checks tree when bootError set. So the app WORKS but shows an error card. Before the PR: spinner until 12s then app. So the PR introduces a regression for slow-first-render apps. It's a real edge case worth flagging as IMPORTANT.

Also restart with bootError never cleared: if restart is a real path (the doc comment says "Starts (or restarts)"), a fixed widget stays on the error card. Let me verify restart usage.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit

- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other

  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);

  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are

  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +271
- **Deletions**: -121
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T19:54:44Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336

    "description": "## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.

Post-merge/CI.
